A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same JacobianODE research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original dynamical-system simulations, Jacobian-estimation benchmarks, task-trained RNN control experiments, ablations, and computational timing measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds an echo-state-network comparison and empirical analyses of Jacobian rank and manifold dimensionality.

M1.justification: The Jacobian network, derivative reconstruction through path integration, trajectory and loop-closure losses, teacher forcing, and inference procedure are retained. Expanded explanations and relocated equations do not establish an algorithmic change; gradient clipping is newly disclosed implementation information.

E1.justification: The dynamical systems and working-memory task remain unchanged. However, new Appendix C.6 explicitly describes ESN Jacobian evaluation on Lorenz test data with 1% observation noise, adding a limited test-input condition beyond the noise-free Jacobian evaluation described in Section 4.

E2.justification: Appendix C.6 adds an actually evaluated echo state network comparator for Lorenz prediction and Jacobian estimation. The existing NeuralODE, weighted-linear, larger residual NeuralODE, and control-task comparators are retained.

E3.justification: The added ESN experiment introduces a 300-node reservoir, 150-step prediction lead-up, and 7,200-step Jacobian lead-up with true-state conditioning. Appendix C.7 adds rank and participation-ratio evaluation using pooled states and flattened Jacobians. Existing benchmark splits, training budgets, and control protocols are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.7 tests whether low-dimensional structure could explain performance, examining matrix rank and intrinsic dimensionality in the RNN and 64-dimensional Lorenz 96 system. The component ablations and NeuralODE architecture/inference-time analyses in C.4-C.5 are retained.

E5.justification: The five-initialization mean-plus-standard-deviation convention, trajectory-based SD/SE, ten timing repetitions, and t-test/Wilcoxon procedures remain unchanged. Revised captions clarify the existing variability source; the added ESN result uses the same five-seed reporting convention.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the matched earlier supplementary tables retain their numerical values. C.6 adds ESN prediction MSE 0.03 and Jacobian Frobenius error 85.8 ± 3.1. C.7 adds manifold participation ratios of approximately 13.5/6 for RNN states/Jacobians and 47.5/50 for Lorenz 96. The ESN test-noise description limits direct comparison with the clean-test benchmark.

T1.justification: Proposition 1 and its proof, the Gramian derivation, subsystem extensions, and loop-closure error-bound derivation remain substantively unchanged. Mathematical material moved between the main text and appendices is retained; notation corrections and explanatory additions do not introduce new formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: direct Jacobian estimation, nonlinear subsystem-control analysis, learning-dependent RNN interactions, and accurate behavioral control. The added evidence does not redefine or strengthen these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds specific cautions about fine-grained reachability estimates and untested scaling to thousands of neurons. It also explains how loop constraints inform directions outside the observed flow, discusses ESN Jacobian nonuniqueness, and interprets the RNN's low-dimensional manifolds alongside the higher-dimensional Lorenz 96 results.

D1.justification: D.8.5 newly discloses gradient-norm clipping at 1.0. Added sections document ESN implementation and dimensionality-analysis procedures, while figure captions specify spectral embedding. The new checklist states that submission code and data were supplied, but does not establish a public release from the PDFs alone.

R1.justification: v2 retains the original 138 cited works and adds five references supporting reservoir-computing comparisons and neural-dimensionality context. These extend the positioning locally; moving Related Work earlier does not itself change its scientific content.

P1.justification: The main narrative is substantially reorganized: Related Work moves before the method, the analytical framework is split between method and RNN-control sections, and detailed derivative/loss equations move into Appendix A. Method explanations are rewritten, RNN/control exposition is expanded, and a conference checklist is appended.

P2.justification: Figures 2-3 are rearranged, and Figures 4-6 and S2 receive extensive label, axis, legend, and spacing revisions. State-space and RNN-weight illustrations are replaced. New Tables S1-S2 tabulate metrics previously plotted, accompanying removal of crowded numerical plot labels. This substantially revises the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 improves readability, makes existing metrics easier to inspect, and adds useful dimensionality evidence and specific reachability/scalability qualifications. Additional implementation details also improve reproducibility. These are limited gains over an already extensively documented study: the principal results and proofs remain unchanged, and the ESN comparison's differing test-noise description prevents treating its reported gap as a fully matched comparison.
